target: Han tappar alltid bort nycklarna och lägger sedan tjugo minuter på att leta.
english: He always loses the keys and then spends twenty minutes looking for them.
tip: tappa bort means to lose or misplace, and alltid splits it: tappar alltid bort.

target: Hon har jobbat som lärare sedan hon tog examen.
english: She has worked as a teacher since she graduated.
tip: After som a profession takes no article: jobbat som lärare, worked as a teacher.
lite grann is a fixed phrase meaning a tiny bit; grann here is not the word for neighbor.
For body parts Swedish uses the definite form, so bröt armen means broke his arm, not bröt sin arm.
Days of the week are not capitalized in Swedish.
Start with a time word like Imorgon and the verb är comes before the subject det.
hem means toward home for motion; being located at home is hemma.
vuxit is the irregular supine of växa (to grow), the form used after har.
After är a predicate adjective adds -a for a plural subject: vi är glada.
sett is the irregular supine of se (to see), the form used after har.
vunnit is the supine of vinna; strong verbs shift the i to u here.
Clock times use klockan: landar klockan tre means lands at three.
inga is the plural of ingen: inga direktflyg means no direct flights.
A definite adjective needs both a front word and a noun ending: det lilla barnet.
hela is followed by a definite noun with no extra article: hela dagen, the whole day.
skrivit is the supine of skriva (to write), the form used after har.
mitt is the my form for ett-words: mitt lösenord; en-words take min instead.
sin means one's own and refers back to the subject: sin plånbok is her own wallet.
att before a verb marks the infinitive, like English to: att flytta means to move.
tänka pairs with på for about: tänkt på saken means thought about the matter.

target: Jag har hört talas om det.
tip: hört talas om is a set phrase meaning to have heard about something.

target: Han undrade vem som hade ringt.
tip: When vem is the subject of an embedded clause it takes som: vem som hade ringt.

target: Det finns hundra platser ibland här.
english: There are a hundred seats sometimes here.
tip: "Det finns" (there is/are) works for both singular and plural in Swedish.

target: Det tar ungefär en timme med bil.
english: It takes about an hour by car.
tip: After med a means of transport drops its article: med bil means by car.

target: Vi stannade hemma för att det snöade.
english: We stayed home because it was snowing.
tip: "För att" = because (reason). Not to be confused with "för att" = in order to (purpose).

target: Om jag hade vetat hade jag kommit.
english: If I had known I would have come.
tip: Past unreal conditions use hade plus the supine in both halves: hade vetat, hade kommit.

target: Innan du går, kan du stänga fönstret?
english: Before you go, can you close the window?
tip: Innan means before and opens a time clause: Innan du går, before you leave.

target: Nu när du är här kan vi börja.
english: Now that you're here we can start.
tip: Nu när means now that, setting up a current reason: Nu när du är här.

target: Jag vet inte om han kommer till slut.
english: I don't know if he's coming in the end.
tip: "Om" = if/whether in subordinate clauses. Different from "om" = about.

target: Vi har redan bestämt oss för resemålet nästa sommar.
english: We have already decided on the travel destination for next summer.
tip: bestämma sig för means decide on, needing the reflexive oss and för: bestämt oss för.
